pali: the citta. When effort or energy is kusala it is the condition for courage and perseverance in the performing of kusala. Energy is right effort of the eightfold Path when it accompanies right understanding of the eightfold Path. It is the condition for perseverance with the investi-gation and study of the reality appearing at the present moment, be it a mental phenomenon or a physical phenomenon. Energy and pa-tience are indispensable for the development of right understanding. There must be awareness of mental phenomena and physical phenom-ena over and over again, in the course of many lives, so that right understanding can see realities as they are, as impermanent, dukkha and non-self. When we hear the word effort we may have a concept of self who exerts an effort to develop right understanding. Effort is non-self, it is a mental factor which assists right understanding. When there is mindfulness of a reality and understanding investigates its na-ture, right effort arises as well and performs its own function. It does not arise because of one’s wish, it arises because of its own conditions. Right mindfulness is another factor of the eightfold Path. As Iex-plained in chapter seven, there are many levels of mindfulness. There is mindfulness with each kusala citta and its function is to be heed-ful, non-forgetful of what is wholesome. Mindfulness is a factor of the eightfold Path when it accompanies right understanding of the eight-fold Path. There may be theoretical understanding of realities ac-quired through reading and thinking. One may think in the right way of the phenomena of life which are impermanent and non-self. How-ever, in order to directly experience the truth there must be mindful-ness of the reality which appears at the present moment. The moment of mindfulness is extremely short, it falls away immediately. However, during that moment understanding can investigate the characteristic of the reality which appears, and in this way understanding can de-velop very gradually. Right understanding arises together with right mindfulness, but they have each a different function. Right mindful-ness is heedful or attentive to the reality which appears but it does not investigate its nature. It is the function of right understanding to investigate and penetrate the true nature of the reality which appears at the present moment.
pt: o citta. Quando o esforço ou energia é kusala, é a condição para a coragem e a perseverança na realização do kusala. A energia é o esforço correto do Caminho Óctuplo quando acompanha o entendimento correto do Caminho Óctuplo. É a condição para a perseverança com a investigação e o estudo da realidade que aparece no momento presente, seja ela uma realidade mental ou uma realidade física. Energia e paciência são indispensáveis para o desenvolvimento do entendimento correto. Deve haver atenção às realidades mentais e realidades físicas repetidas vezes, no curso de muitas vidas, de modo que o entendimento correto possa ver as realidades como elas são, como impermanentes, dukkha e não-eu. Quando ouvimos a palavra esforço, podemos ter um conceito de eu que exerce um esforço para desenvolver o entendimento correto. O esforço é não-eu, é um fator mental que auxilia o entendimento correto. Quando há a atenção plena de uma realidade e o entendimento investiga a sua natureza, o esforço correto surge também e desempenha a sua própria função. Não surge por causa do desejo de alguém, surge devido às suas próprias condições. A atenção plena correta é outro fator do Caminho Óctuplo. Como expliquei no capítulo sete, há muitos níveis de atenção plena. Há atenção plena com cada citta kusala e sua função é ser atenta, não esquecida daquilo que é benéfico. A atenção plena é um fator do Caminho Óctuplo quando acompanha o entendimento correto do Caminho Óctuplo. Pode haver um entendimento teórico de realidades adquirido por meio da leitura e do pensamento. Pode-se pensar da maneira correta sobre as realidades da vida que são impermanentes e não-eu. Entretanto, a fim de experimentar diretamente a verdade, deve haver a atenção plena da realidade que aparece no momento presente. O momento da atenção plena é extremamente curto, ele desaparece imediatamente. Entretanto, durante esse momento, o entendimento pode investigar a característica da realidade que aparece e, desta maneira, o entendimento pode desenvolver-se muito gradualmente. O entendimento correto surge junto com a atenção plena correta, mas eles têm cada um uma função diferente. A atenção plena correta é atenta ou vigilante em relação à realidade que aparece, mas ela não investiga sua natureza. É a função do entendimento correto investigar e penetrar a verdadeira natureza da realidade que aparece no momento presente.

es: el citta. Cuando el esfuerzo o la energía es kusala, es la condición para el coraje y la perseverancia en la realización de kusala. La energía es el esfuerzo correcto del Camino Óctuple cuando acompaña al entendimiento correcto del Camino Óctuple. Es la condición para la perseverancia en la investigación y el estudio de la realidad que aparece en el momento presente, ya sea una realidad mental o una realidad física. La energía y la paciencia son indispensables para el desarrollo del entendimiento correcto. Debe haber atención a las realidades mentales y a las realidades físicas una y otra vez, a lo largo de muchas vidas, para que el entendimiento correcto pueda ver las realidades tal como son, como impermanentes, dukkha y no-yo. Cuando oímos la palabra esfuerzo, podemos tener el concepto de un yo que ejerce un esfuerzo para desarrollar el entendimiento correcto. El esfuerzo es no-yo; es un factor mental que ayuda al entendimiento correcto. Cuando hay atención plena de una realidad y el entendimiento investiga su naturaleza, el esfuerzo correcto también surge y cumple su propia función. No surge debido al deseo de uno, surge debido a sus propias condiciones. La atención plena correcta es otro factor del Camino Óctuple. Como expliqué en el capítulo siete, hay muchos niveles de atención plena. Hay atención plena con cada citta kusala y su función es ser diligente, no olvidadiza de lo que es beneficioso. La atención plena es un factor del Camino Óctuple cuando acompaña al entendimiento correcto del Camino Óctuple. Puede haber una comprensión teórica de las realidades adquirida a través de la lectura y la reflexión. Uno puede pensar de manera correcta sobre las realidades de la vida que son impermanentes y no-yo. Sin embargo, para experimentar directamente la verdad debe haber atención plena de la realidad que aparece en el momento presente. El momento de atención plena es sumamente breve, desaparece de inmediato. Sin embargo, durante ese momento el entendimiento puede investigar la característica de la realidad que aparece, y de este modo el entendimiento puede desarrollarse muy gradualmente. El entendimiento correcto surge junto con la atención plena correcta, pero cada uno tiene una función diferente. La atención plena correcta es diligente o atenta a la realidad que aparece, pero no investiga su naturaleza. La función del entendimiento correcto es investigar y penetrar la verdadera naturaleza de la realidad que aparece en el momento presente.

pali: Right concentration is another factor of the eightfold Path. Con-centration or one-pointedness is a mental factor arising with each citta. Citta experiences only one object at a time and concentration has the function to focus on that one object which citta experiences. Concen-tration can accompany kusala citta, akusala citta and citta which is neither kusala nor akusala. Right concentration is concentration which is wholesome. Right concentration is of many kinds and degrees. As we have seen in chapter seven, there is right concentration in tranquil meditation. When calm is developed to the extent that absorption is attained, there is a high degree of concentration which focuses on the meditation subject. Sense-cognitions such as seeing or hearing do not arise and defilements are temporarily subdued. There is also right concentration in the development of direct understanding of realities. The Path factor right concentration accompanies right understanding of the eightfold Path. It focuses rightly on the reality which appears at the present moment and which is the object of right understanding. It is not necessary to make a special effort to concentrate on mental phenomena and physical phenomena. If one tries to concentrate one clings to an idea of “my concentration”, and then right understanding is not being developed. When there are conditions for the arising of right mindfulness and right understanding, there is right concentration already which focuses on the reality presenting itself at that moment. Some people believe that one should first develop morality, after that concentration and then right understanding. However, all kinds of kusala, be it generosity, good moral conduct or calm can develop together with right understanding. There is no particular order in the development of wholesomeness. Kusala citta is non-self, anattā. When one reads the scriptures one will come across texts on the development of right concentration which has reached the stage of absorption. This does not imply that all people should develop calm to the degree of absorption. As Iexplained in chapter seven, it depends on the individ-ual’ s accumulations whether he can develop it or not. The Buddha encouraged those who could develop calm to the degree of absorp-tion to be mindful of realities in order to see also absorption as non self. pt: A concentração correta é outro fator do Caminho Óctuplo. A concentração, ou o foco em um único ponto, é um fator mental que surge com cada citta. O citta experimenta apenas um objeto de cada vez e a concentração tem a função de focar naquele único objeto que o citta experimenta. A concentração pode acompanhar o citta kusala, o citta akusala e o citta que não é nem kusala nem akusala. A concentração correta é a concentração que é benéfica. A concentração correta é de muitos tipos e graus. Como vimos no capítulo sete, há a concentração correta na meditação de tranquilidade. Quando a calma é desenvolvida ao ponto em que a absorção é atingida, há um alto grau de concentração que foca no tema de meditação. As cognições sensoriais, tais como ver ou ouvir, não surgem, e as contaminações são temporariamente subjugadas. Há também a concentração correta no desenvolvimento do entendimento direto de realidades. O fator do Caminho concentração correta acompanha o entendimento correto do Caminho Óctuplo. Ela foca corretamente na realidade que aparece no momento presente e que é o objeto do entendimento correto. Não é necessário fazer um esforço especial para se concentrar em realidades mentais e realidades físicas. Se alguém tenta se concentrar, se apega a uma ideia de "minha concentração", e então o entendimento correto não está sendo desenvolvido. Quando há condições para o surgimento da atenção plena correta e do entendimento correto, já existe a concentração correta que foca na realidade que se apresenta naquele momento. es: La concentración correcta es otro factor del Camino Óctuple. La concentración o unifocalización es un factor mental que surge con cada citta. El citta experimenta solo un objeto a la vez y la concentración tiene la función de enfocarse en ese único objeto que el citta experimenta. La concentración puede acompañar al citta kusala, al citta akusala y al citta que no es ni kusala ni akusala. La concentración correcta es la concentración que es beneficiosa. La concentración correcta es de muchas clases y grados. Como hemos visto en el capítulo siete, hay concentración correcta en la meditación de tranquilidad. Cuando la calma se desarrolla hasta el punto de alcanzar la absorción, hay un alto grado de concentración que se enfoca en el tema de meditación. Las cogniciones sensoriales, tales como ver u oír, no surgen y las contaminaciones quedan temporalmente subyugadas. También hay concentración correcta en el desarrollo del entendimiento directo de las realidades. El factor del Camino de la concentración correcta acompaña al entendimiento correcto del Camino Óctuple. Se enfoca correctamente en la realidad que aparece en el momento presente y que es el objeto del entendimiento correcto. No es necesario hacer un esfuerzo especial para concentrarse en realidades mentales y realidades físicas. Si uno intenta concentrarse, se apega a la idea de «mi concentración», y entonces el entendimiento correcto no se está desarrollando. Cuando hay condiciones para el surgimiento de la atención plena correcta y del entendimiento correcto, ya existe la concentración correcta que se enfoca en la realidad que se presenta en ese momento. Algunas personas creen que primero se debería desarrollar la moralidad, después la concentración y luego el entendimiento correcto. Sin embargo, toda clase de kusala, ya sea generosidad, buena conducta moral o calma, puede desarrollarse junto con el entendimiento correcto. No hay un orden particular en el desarrollo de lo beneficioso. El citta kusala es no-yo, anattā. Cuando uno lee las escrituras, encuentra textos sobre el desarrollo de la concentración correcta que ha alcanzado la etapa de absorción. Esto no implica que todas las personas deban desarrollar la calma hasta el grado de absorción. Como expliqué en el capítulo siete, depende de las acumulaciones del individuo si puede desarrollarla o no. El Buda animó a quienes podían desarrollar la calma hasta el grado de absorción a estar atentos a las realidades a fin de ver también la absorción como no-yo. En ella hay innumerables matices y variaciones de significado. Innumerables son las formas de ilustrar esta noble verdad de: Esta es la práctica que conduce a la cesación de dukkha. Por lo tanto, monjes, debe hacerse un esfuerzo para comprender: Esto es dukkha; Este es el origen de dukkha; Esta es la cesación de dukkha; Esta es la práctica que conduce a la cesación de dukkha». El Camino Óctuple debe desarrollarse en la vida diaria. Uno debe llegar a conocer todas las realidades, también las propias contaminaciones, tal como surgen debido a sus propias condiciones. Uno no puede cambiar la realidad que surge; es no-yo. Inevitablemente surgirán malentendidos respecto al desarrollo del entendimiento correcto si no se ha comprendido correctamente cuáles son los objetos de la atención plena y del entendimiento correcto. Por lo tanto, deseo enfatizar algunos puntos relativos a estos objetos. Algunas personas creen que un lugar tranquilo es más favorable para el desarrollo del entendimiento correcto. Deberían examinarse a sí mismas para descubrir qué tipos de citta motivan su pensamiento. Si los laicos quieren vivir como monjes para tener más oportunidades de desarrollar el entendimiento correcto, son guiados por el deseo. Es debido a condiciones, a las inclinaciones acumuladas de cada uno, que uno sea monje o laico. Tanto el monje como el laico pueden desarrollar el entendimiento, cada uno en su propia situación. Entonces uno llegará a comprender sus propias inclinaciones acumuladas. El desarrollo del Camino Óctuple es el desarrollo del entendimiento correcto de todas las realidades que surgen debido a sus propias condiciones, también del propio apego, de la aversión y de otras contaminaciones. A fin de recordar a las personas las realidades que pueden ser objetos de atención plena y de entendimiento correcto, el Buda enseñó las «Cuatro Aplicaciones de la Atención Plena». Estas Cuatro Aplicaciones contienen todas las realidades mentales y realidades físicas de la vida diaria que

pali: can be objects of mindfulness and right understanding. They are: Contemplation of the Body, which comprises all physical phenomena, Contemplation of Feeling, Contemplation of Citta and Contemplation of Dhammas, which comprises all realities not included in the other three Applications of Mindfulness. pali: ther explanation of objects of mindfulness which present themselves in daily life. Some people believe that mindfulness is being conscious of what one is doing. If one is conscious of what one is doing, such as reading or walking, there is thinking of concepts, no awareness of realities. There is clinging to an idea of self who reads or walks. No matter what one is doing there are mental phenomena and physical phenomena and understanding of them can be developed. When one, for example, is watching T.V., one may think of a story which is being enacted. However, there is not only thinking, Also seeing, visible ob-ject, hearing, sound, feeling or remembrance arise. Most of the time there is forgetfulness of realities, one thinks of concepts. However, in between the moments of thinking mindfulness can arise of one reality appearing through one of the six doors, an ultimate reality which is either a mental reality or a physical reality. The characteristics of dif-ferent realities can gradually be understood. When we read a book we think of the meaning of the letters and of the story. But there are also moments of seeing merely what is visible, of what appears through eyesense. It is because of remembrance that we know the meaning of what we read. Remembrance is a mental factor arising together with the citta, it is not self. Also remembrance can be understood as it is. It seems that thinking occurs at the same time as seeing, but they are different cittas with different characteristics. The char-acteristics of different realities can be investigated, no matter whether we are seeing, reading, hearing or paying attention to the meaning of words. When this has been understood we will see that objects of awareness are never lacking in our daily life. There are six doorways, there are objects experienced through these six doorways and there are the realities which experience these objects. That is our life. There are several stages of insight in the course of the development of right understanding. Even the first stage of insight, which is merely a beginning stage of insight, is difficult to reach. At this stage the different characteristics of the mental real-ity and of the physical reality which appear are clearly distinguished from each other. pali: comes keener. The objects of understanding are the same: the mental phenomena and physical phenomena which appear, but understand-ing of them becomes clearer. When conditioned realities have been clearly understood as impermanent, dukkha and non-self, nibbāna, the unconditioned reality, can be experienced. The citta which expe-riences nibbāna is a “supramundane” citta4 , it is of a plane of citta which is higher than the plane of cittas which experience sense ob-jects or the plane of cittas with absorption. All eight Path factors accompany the supramundane citta at the moment of enlightenment. Defilements are subsequently eradicated at four stages of enlighten-ment. The supramundane cittas which experience nibbāna arise and then fall away immediately. When the fourth and final stage of en-lightenment has not been attained, defilements arise again. However, the person who has attained even the first stage of enlightenment has no more conditions to commit akusala kamma to the degree that it can produce rebirth in an unhappy plane of existence. When one reads the words “enlightenment” and “supramundane”, one may imagine that enlightenment is something mysterious, that it cannot occur in daily life. However, it is the function of right un-derstanding to penetrate the true nature of realities in daily life, and when it has been developed to the degree that enlightenment can be attained, the supramundane citta which experiences nibbāna can arise in daily life. Enlightenment can be attained even shortly after akusala citta has arisen, if right understanding has penetrated its true nature. We read in the Psalms of the Sisters (Therı̄gāthā, Canto I, 1) that a woman attained enlightenment in the kitchen. When she noticed that the curry was burnt in the oven she realized the characteristic of impermanence inherent in conditioned realities and then attained enlightenment. We read that people in the Buddha’s time could attain enlightenment even while they were hearing the Buddha preach or just after his sermon. One may wonder how they could attain enlightenment so quickly. They had accumulated the right conditions 4 In Pāli: lokuttara citta.

pali: household life. All kinds of wholesomeness are forms of renunciation, of detachment. One renounces clinging to oneself, to one ’s own com-fort. Akitti renounced his own comfort when he went without food for three days. Akitti accumulated the Perfection of wisdom. The Perfection of wisdom is not only right understanding of the eightfold Path, it comprises all levels of wisdom. The Bodhisatta, even when he was an animal, accumulated the Perfection of wisdom. He knew akusala as akusala, kusala as kusala, he knew the right conditions for the attainment of Buddhahood. When he gave food to the brahman, there was energy or courage, which is indispensable for each kind of kusala. Energy strengthens the kusala citta so that good deeds can be performed. He had patience, he was glad to endure hunger for three days, and had there be an opportunity for a longer period of time to give away his food, he would have fasted longer, even for one or two months. He also accumulated the Perfection of truthfulness. Truthful-ness has several aspects. It is not only truthfulness in speech but also sincerity in action and thought. Kusala must be known as kusala and akusala as akusala. One should not delude oneself with regard to one’s faults and vices, even when they are more subtle. It should be known that when one is giving a gift with selfish motives, there is no sincere inclination to kusala, that one may take akusala for kusala. Akitti had a sincere inclination to give and did not expect any benefit for himself. The Perfection of truthfulness is indispensable for the development of right understanding. One has to be sincere with regard to what one has understood and what one has not understood yet, otherwise there cannot be any progress. The Bodhisatta accumulated determination, he had an unshakable determination to persevere with the develop-ment of understanding and the other Perfections until he would reach the goal. He had loving kindness, he thought of the brahman’s welfare, not of himself. There was equanimity, he had no aversion even though he went without food for three days. He had equanimity towards the vicissitudes of life. Right understanding of kamma and the result of kamma conditions equanimity. This text illustrates that the Perfections can be accumulated when a good deed is being performed. As we have seen, there are ten kinds of good qualities which have been classified as the Perfections. Good

pali: qualities are not always Perfections. They are Perfections only when the aim of the performing of kusala is the diminishing of defilements and eventually their eradication at enlightenment. The accumulation of the ten Perfections together with the development of right under-standing of realities is the application of the Buddha’s teachings in daily life. There may not be mindfulness of ultimate realities very often, but there are many opportunities to accumulate other kinds of kusala, the Perfections. It is encouraging to know that all kinds and levels of kusala can be Perfections, helpful conditions to reach the goal. Even when we help other people in giving them good advice or in consoling them when they are in distress can be an opportunity for the accumulation of the Perfections, conditions to diminish selfishness and other defilements. The development of the eightfold Path which leads to enlighten-ment seems to be far-fetched for an ordinary person. It is such a long way before the goal can be reached. There will be more confidence in the Buddha’s teachings when one sees that what he taught can be verified and applied in one’s own life. The development of under-standing can only be very gradual, just as learning a new skill such as a foreign language has to be very gradual. The Perfection of pa-tience is indispensable for the development of right understanding of realities. Learning about the Path-factors which each perform their own function helps us to see that no self, no person develops right understanding. We do not have to adopt a particular life-style for the development of understanding. Understanding can develop when it is assisted by the other Path-factors and supported by other conditions, including the Perfections. There should be no discouragement about the long way which lies ahead. There can at least be a beginning of understanding of the reality appearing at the present moment through one of the six doors. The Buddha taught the conditions for the development of what is good and wholesome and the conditions for the eradication of de-filements. In developing the Buddha’s Path one will come to know one’s ignorance of realities, one’s selfishness and other defilements. The change from selfishness to detachment, from ignorance to under-standing is immense. How could such changes take place within a
pt: qualidades não são sempre Perfeições. Elas são Perfeições somente quando o objetivo da realização de kusala é a diminuição das contaminações e, eventualmente, sua erradicação na iluminação. A acumulação das dez Perfeições juntamente com o desenvolvimento do entendimento correto das realidades é a aplicação dos ensinamentos do Buda na vida diária. Pode não haver atenção plena às realidades últimas com muita frequência, mas há muitas oportunidades para acumular outros tipos de kusala, as Perfeições. É encorajador saber que todos os tipos e níveis de kusala podem ser Perfeições, condições úteis para alcançar o objetivo. Mesmo quando ajudamos outras pessoas dando-lhes bons conselhos ou consolando-as quando elas estão angustiadas pode ser uma oportunidade para a acumulação das Perfeições, condições para diminuir o egoísmo e outras contaminações. O desenvolvimento do Caminho Óctuplo, que leva à iluminação, parece algo distante para uma pessoa comum. É um longo caminho antes que o objetivo possa ser alcançado. Haverá mais confiança nos ensinamentos do Buda quando se vir que o que ele ensinou pode ser verificado e aplicado na própria vida de alguém. O desenvolvimento do entendimento só pode ser muito gradual, assim como o aprendizado de uma nova habilidade, como um idioma estrangeiro, tem de ser muito gradual. A Perfeição da paciência é indispensável para o desenvolvimento do entendimento correto das realidades. Aprender sobre os fatores do Caminho, cada um desempenhando sua própria função, nos ajuda a ver que nenhum eu, nenhuma pessoa desenvolve o entendimento correto. Não precisamos adotar um estilo de vida específico para o desenvolvimento do entendimento. O entendimento pode se desenvolver quando é auxiliado pelos outros fatores do Caminho e apoiado por outras condições, incluindo as Perfeições. Não deve haver desânimo sobre o longo caminho que está pela frente. Pode haver, pelo menos, um começo do entendimento da realidade que aparece no momento presente através de uma das seis portas. O Buda ensinou as condições para o desenvolvimento do que é bom e benéfico e as condições para a erradicação das contaminações. Ao desenvolver o Caminho do Buda, a pessoa virá a conhecer a sua própria ignorância das realidades, o seu próprio egoísmo e outras contaminações. en: qualities are not always Perfections. They are Perfections only when the aim of the performing of kusala is the diminishing of defilements and eventually their eradication at enlightenment. The accumulation of the ten Perfections together with the development of right understanding of realities is the application of the Buddha’s teachings in daily life. There may not be mindfulness of ultimate realities very often, but there are many opportunities to accumulate other kinds of kusala, the Perfections. It is encouraging to know that all kinds and levels of kusala can be Perfections, helpful conditions to reach the goal. Even when we help other people in giving them good advice or in consoling them when they are in distress can be an opportunity for the accumulation of the Perfections, conditions to diminish selfishness and other defilements. The development of the eightfold Path which leads to enlightenment seems to be far-fetched for an ordinary person. It is such a long way before the goal can be reached. There will be more confidence in the Buddha’s teachings when one sees that what he taught can be verified and applied in one’s own life. The development of understanding can only be very gradual, just as learning a new skill such as a foreign language has to be very gradual. The Perfection of patience is indispensable for the development of right understanding of realities. Learning about the Path-factors which each perform their own function helps us to see that no self, no person develops right understanding. We do not have to adopt a particular life-style for the development of understanding. Understanding can develop when it is assisted by the other Path-factors and supported by other conditions, including the Perfections. There should be no discouragement about the long way which lies ahead. There can at least be a beginning of understanding of the reality appearing at the present moment through one of the six doors. The Buddha taught the conditions for the development of what is good and wholesome and the conditions for the eradication of defilements. In developing the Buddha’s Path one will come to know one’s ignorance of realities, one’s selfishness and other defilements. The change from selfishness to detachment, from ignorance to understanding is immense. How could such changes take place within a
es: cualidades no siempre son Perfecciones. Son Perfecciones únicamente cuando el propósito de realizar kusala es la disminución de las contaminaciones y eventualmente su erradicación en la iluminación. La acumulación de las diez Perfecciones junto con el desarrollo del entendimiento correcto de las realidades es la aplicación de las enseñanzas del Buda en la vida diaria. Puede que no haya atención plena a las realidades últimas muy a menudo, pero hay muchas oportunidades para acumular otras clases de kusala, las Perfecciones. Es alentador saber que todas las clases y niveles de kusala pueden ser Perfecciones, condiciones provechosas para alcanzar la meta. Incluso cuando ayudamos a otras personas dándoles un buen consejo o consolándolas cuando están afligidas, puede ser una oportunidad para la acumulación de las Perfecciones, condiciones para disminuir el egoísmo y otras contaminaciones. El desarrollo del Camino Óctuple que conduce a la iluminación parece muy lejano para una persona común. Hay un camino tan largo antes de que se pueda alcanzar la meta. Habrá más confianza en las enseñanzas del Buda cuando uno vea que lo que él enseñó puede verificarse y aplicarse en la propia vida. El desarrollo del entendimiento solo puede ser muy gradual, al igual que aprender una nueva habilidad, como un idioma extranjero, tiene que ser muy gradual. La Perfección de la paciencia es indispensable para el desarrollo del entendimiento correcto de las realidades. Aprender acerca de los factores del Camino que cumplen cada uno su propia función nos ayuda a ver que ningún yo, ninguna persona desarrolla el entendimiento correcto. No tenemos que adoptar un estilo de vida particular para el desarrollo del entendimiento. El entendimiento puede desarrollarse cuando es asistido por los demás factores del Camino y apoyado por otras condiciones, incluidas las Perfecciones. No debería haber desánimo por el largo camino que queda por delante. Puede haber al menos un comienzo de entendimiento de la realidad que aparece en el momento presente a través de una de las seis puertas. El Buda enseñó las condiciones para el desarrollo de lo que es bueno y saludable, y las condiciones para la erradicación de las contaminaciones. Al desarrollar el Camino del Buda, uno llegará a conocer la propia ignorancia de las realidades, el propio egoísmo y las demás contaminaciones. pali: Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating four noble Truths that we have run on, wandered on, this long, long road, both you and I. What are the four? Through not understanding, not penetrating the noble truth of dukkha, of the arising of dukkha, of the ceasing of dukkha, of the way leading to the ceasing of dukkha, we have run on, wandered on, this long long road, both you and I. But now, monks, the noble truth of dukkha is understood, is penetrated, likewise the noble truth of the arising, of the ceasing of dukkha, of the way leading to the ceasing of dukkha is understood, is penetrated. Uprooted is the crav-ing to exist, destroyed is the channel to becoming, there is no more coming to be. . .
pt: Monges, é por não entendermos, não penetrarmos as quatro Nobres Verdades que nós corremos, vagamos, nessa longa, longa estrada, tanto vocês quanto eu. Quais são as quatro? Por não entender, não penetrar a nobre verdade de dukkha, do surgimento de dukkha, da cessação de dukkha, do caminho que conduz à cessação de dukkha, nós corremos, vagamos, por essa longa, longa estrada, tanto vocês quanto eu. Mas agora, monges, a nobre verdade de dukkha foi entendida, foi penetrada, da mesma forma a nobre verdade do surgimento, da cessação de dukkha, do caminho que conduz à cessação de dukkha foi entendida, foi penetrada. Arrancado pela raiz foi o anseio de existir, destruído foi o canal para o devir, não há mais vir a ser...
en: Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating four noble Truths that we have run on, wandered on, this long, long road, both you and I. What are the four? Through not understanding, not penetrating the noble truth of dukkha, of the arising of dukkha, of the ceasing of dukkha, of the way leading to the ceasing of dukkha, we have run on, wandered on, this long long road, both you and I. But now, monks, the noble truth of dukkha is understood, is penetrated, likewise the noble truth of the arising, of the ceasing of dukkha, of the way leading to the ceasing of dukkha is understood, is penetrated. Uprooted is the craving to exist, destroyed is the channel to becoming, there is no more coming to be. . .
es: «Monjes, es por no comprender, por no penetrar las cuatro nobles Verdades que hemos corrido, que hemos vagado por este largo, largo camino, tanto vosotros como yo. ¿Cuáles son las cuatro? Por no comprender, por no penetrar la noble verdad de dukkha, del surgimiento de dukkha, de la cesación de dukkha, del camino que conduce a la cesación de dukkha, hemos corrido, hemos vagado por este largo, largo camino, tanto vosotros como yo. Pero ahora, monjes, la noble verdad de dukkha ha sido comprendida, ha sido penetrada; de la misma manera la noble verdad del surgimiento, de la cesación de dukkha, del camino que conduce a la cesación de dukkha ha sido comprendida, ha sido penetrada. Arrancado de raíz está el anhelo de existir, destruido está el cauce hacia el devenir, ya no hay más devenir...»
